question: Does a fixed per-action mean-delta base plus a closed-form ridge residual on native taps beat copy, mean-delta and shuffled controls on calibration and test, without retention loss?

arms.full: ridge on the full 1024-d rms-normalized tap, centered per action on train
arms.proj: ridge on the 16-d fixed projection z = x @ p

lambda_grid: lambda = s * trace(K)/n for s in [0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000] plus inf (= mean-delta control); per action, chosen on calibration MSE only, ties to stronger regularization

gates.normal_equations: max relative residual of (F^T F + lam I) W = F^T R below 1e-8 (replaces analytic_gradient; no iterative training)
gates.noncollapse: unchanged formula; target is the fixed projection, so it cannot fail by construction (declared, not evidence)
gates.predictive_gain_over_controls: unchanged: per action prediction < .98 * min(copy, mean_delta, shuffled) on calibration and test
gates.fixed_reference_retention: unchanged: per action retention MSE <= mean-delta control (delta 0)

decision_rule: A run passes only if all gates hold. Test partitions of rounds 3-5 are already exposed (results of rounds 3-5 were read), so even a pass is only a hint and would need a fresh capture (round 7) before any claim about §99. Failures are kept and reported unchanged; no grid or gate change after this registration.
not_changed: No file under code/v13/ changed; no runtime, receiver or learn authority.
